summary: Discovery for Dedicated GPU capacity. Brighthaven needs predictable throughput for low-latency customer-facing LLM features, strict data isolation, and burst capacity for peak trading windows. Key concerns: network isolation/VPC, SOC2/KMS, autoscaling and cost tradeoffs. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated with benchmark targets; Redwood to send pricing and pilot plan.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 09:23 - 10:05 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Clarke (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morris (Brighthaven Head of ML), Marcus Reed (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Security)

[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Avery from Redwood Inference, and joining me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Elena (Brighthaven): Morning, thanks. We're good. Marcus and Priya are here too.
[00:15] Marcus: morning.
[00:20] Priya: hi.
[00:25] Avery: Great, quick agenda — understand your current stack, latency and throughput targets, security/isolation needs, and then talk through Redwood Dedicated options and next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Elena: Yep, that's what we want to cover. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Our priority is latency and data separation — financial data, PII, trading signals.
[00:45] Samir (Redwood SE): Understood. Can you give a brief on the feature set you plan to run in prod and expected QPS/peak patterns?
[00:55] Elena: Sure. Two main things: 1) customer support assistant that answers account questions with context (medium length prompts, response < 2s target), and 2) a real-time insights stream for traders that generates short snippets — those need sub-1s 95th percentile for single-turn requests. Average concurrency today is ~80 concurrent requests during day, spikes to ~800 during market opens.
[01:20] Marcus: to add, our infra currently runs in GCP us-east1, we use private VPCs and have strict egress rules. We want Dedicated capacity in a VPC and ideally reserved GPUs with predictable throughput.
[01:35] Priya: and SOC2 is in place, we need audit logs, KMS integration for keys, SSO (SAML) and RBAC. We also have an internal procurement timeline — decision in 6 weeks, pilot in 2-3 weeks.
[01:50] Avery: Perfect — that helps. On the Dedicated side, we do reserved GPU pools with options to configure autoscale and burst capacity. Samir, can you talk briefly about the typical capacity constructs?
[02:00] Samir: Yeah. On Redwood Dedicated we provision a reserved pool — you pick GPU type and count, we pin those to your tenant. For burst we can allow controlled bursting into a shared pool or enable temporary extra capacity (burst nodes) — usually gated by a policy. Batching and KV cache also help reduce tokens/cost. Important note: for <1s p95 with short prompts we often recommend H100-class for the right model, or optimized A100 configs if cost constrained.
[02:30] Elena: H100 is expensive though — curious on cost delta and what quantization options exist.
[02:35] Samir: Right, we have quantized variants and runtime paths that reduce costs — 4-bit, mixed precision; tradeoff is potentially a small hit on quality. We'll include model recommendations with the pricing.
[02:50] Marcus: For network isolation — we require a private control plane and everything must go through our VPC peering and private endpoints. Does Redwood support that for Dedicated?
[03:00] Avery: Yes, Redwood Private gives an option for a customer-managed control plane, but Dedicated also supports VPC peering or private endpoints depending on the deployment. We can show the network diagram.
[03:10] Priya: Want to see network architecture and where audit logs and KMS fit. Also air-gapped is a maybe for some sensitive workloads.
[03:20] Samir: We'll share the SOC2 package and the network diagram. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations) — I sometimes see customers call it K N S in notes but it's KMS.
[03:30] Elena: (laughs) yes KMS.
[03:35] Avery: On scaling — how predictable do you need throughput to be vs peak burst? Is it ok to have baseline reserved and allow queued requests during peaks?
[03:45] Elena: Baseline must be resilient — core support assistant can't degrade. For trading snippets, during peak we expect up to 10x baseline for short windows but we need bounded latency. We can't have long tail queuing more than a few hundred ms.
[04:00] Marcus: We also need failover — if Dedicated capacity is saturated we want automatic fallback to a hosted variant or a smaller cheaper model for non-critical requests.
[04:10] Samir: That's common — Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted endpoints as a safety net. You can define per-route SLAs.
[04:25] Elena: Good. How does billing work for reserved + burst? Do we get billed for reserved capacity and separate for burst?
[04:30] Avery: Yes, reserved is a commit (monthly/annual). Burst is either metered or we have a prepaid burst pool option; pricing differs by GPU class. We'll include examples in the quote.
[04:45] Priya: Are we able to limit which models can be deployed to Dedicated for compliance reasons? We want to whitelist model binaries.
[04:50] Samir: Absolutely — Dedicated allows pinned model versions and you can restrict model catalog entries. We also retain model provenance and quantization metadata.
[05:00] Elena: About benchmarks — we need concrete latency and throughput numbers using our prompts. Can Redwood run a benchmark with our prompts and produce token-level latency and cost breakdown?
[05:10] Samir: Yes, we run bench harnesses. For pilot we'll spin up a small Dedicated cluster with your prompts and measure p50/p95 latencies, token throughput, and unit cost. We'll also show KV cache hit rate if you use prefix caching.
[05:30] Marcus: How long to spin up additional capacity? If we need extra GPUs mid-day, what's lead time?
[05:35] Samir: For Dedicated, provisioning typically takes a few hours to a day depending on region and GPU type. We can pre-warm burst nodes. For private/on-prem it's longer.
[05:45] Elena: Security question — where do logs live and who has access?
[05:50] Priya: We need audit logs to go into our SIEM, retention 1 year, and RBAC for access to logs.
[05:58] Samir: Logs can be streamed to your logging endpoints, and audit logs are configurable. We'll provide integration docs.
[06:10] Elena: Are there examples of other finserv customers running under similar constraints?
[06:15] Avery: Yes — we've worked with several banks to run Dedicated + VPC with KMS and auditing. We'll redact names but can include case studies.
[06:25] Marcus: On models — do you host our own fine-tuned weights? We may want to fine-tune on proprietary data.
[06:30] Samir: We support private model artifacts and fine-tuned weights. You can upload artifacts into a private model repo and pin to Dedicated. We can discuss encryption at rest and access controls.
[06:45] Elena: And what's the rollback/fallback story for model rollouts?
[06:50] Samir: We support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback in case of regressions. The console shows per-route metrics and rollout controls.
[07:05] Priya: On compliance — do you have SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001? And do you have penetration testing reports?
[07:12] Avery: We have SOC 2 Type II and are working on ISO; penetration test summaries are available for redacted review. We'll share the package.
[07:25] Elena: Great. For pilot success criteria — we need p95 < 900ms for trading snippets at 500 qps sustained in a 10-minute window, and p95 < 2s for support assistant at 80 qps. Cost target is under $X per 1k requests — we'll give exact numbers in writing.
[07:50] Samir: Noted. We'll design the pilot to hit those targets.
[08:00] Marcus: Ops question — we use Terraform for infra. Does Redwood expose IaC or Terraform modules?
[08:05] Avery: Yes, we provide Terraform modules and an API, plus CloudFormation in some clouds.
[08:12] Elena: Any gotchas around KV cache warm-up and cold starts? If a model needs the KV for context, cold caches can spike latency.
[08:22] Samir: Cache warm-up is important. We'll measure cache hit curves in the benchmark and recommend TTLs and pre-warming strategies. For trading bursts we often combine pre-warm windows and prefix caching.
[08:40] Priya: Can we do a pilot inside our VPC privately?
[08:45] Samir: Yes — we can set up VPC peering and private endpoints for the pilot. For fully air-gapped on-prem it takes longer and is typically part of Private deployment.
[08:55] Elena: Timeline recap — procurement decision in 6 weeks, pilot in 2-3 weeks, procurement docs to be shared with our legal and security.
[09:05] Avery: That aligns. We'll email the quote and SOC2 + network diagrams by Friday. Samir will share a pilot plan and test harness.
[09:15] Marcus: One more thing — can you provide expected headroom metrics per GPU for the models you recommend? We want a sizing table (concurrency per GPU, tokens/sec).
[09:25] Samir: Yes, we'll include a sizing matrix (H100 vs A100 vs G5), with example workloads and expected latency/throughput.
[09:35] Elena: Perfect. I think that's everything.
[09:40] Avery: Thanks everyone — quick recap of next steps: send pricing, send SOC2 + network diagram, pilot plan, schedule kickoff. Any other items?
[09:48] Priya: Please include contact for legal/procurement.
[09:50] Avery: Will do. Thanks all.
[10:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had minor errors (KMS spelled K N S in one spot, some product names like Redwood Private mis-transcribed as Redwood Privatee), speakers sometimes labeled generically in raw export.

- Redwood to send Dedicated pricing with 3 GPU options and burst pricing examples.
- Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II package, network diagram, KMS integration docs.
- SE to prepare pilot benchmark plan using Brighthaven prompts (p95 goals: trading <900ms at 500 qps window; support <2s at 80 qps).
- Schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-16.

References mentioned: pilot benchmark sheet (link to be provided), SOC2 docs, network diagram, Terraform modules.
